stem:
Uday places the fraction $\dfrac{5}{6}$ on a number line marked from $0$ to $1$. The diagram shows that number line.

Which plan places $\dfrac{5}{6}$ correctly?

options.text: Divide the interval from $0$ to $1$ into $6$ equal lengths and count $5$ of those lengths from $0$.
Mark a point near $1$ because the printed $6$ looks large on the page.
The number-line placement rule also requires changing $\dfrac{5}{6}$ into another kind of number first.
Place $\dfrac{5}{6}$ by comparing only how large $5$ looks next to $6$ as a unit fraction of a different whole.

teacher.key_rationale: To place 5/6, partition [0,1] into 6 equal parts and count 5 from 0. Choosing by how large 6 looks is surface capture. Requiring a conversion first over-extends the hinge. Treating the placement as a unit-fraction comparison of a different whole conflates mechanisms.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source right triangle as a 0-to-1 number line partitioned into sixths.
